# Mechanism 1: native SPAKE2+

The native client implements Exacq's mechanism 1 using Edwards25519 and Argon2i.
It selects mechanism 1 when discovery's `NegotiateMechanisms` has bit 1 set;
otherwise bit 0 selects the previously verified P224 mechanism. A failed
mechanism-1 exchange is an authentication error and never triggers a downgrade.
No plaintext password document is sent.

**Verification level:** three known-answer transcripts were generated by
calling the actual pinned Linux SDK's `Spake2PlusClient::Process`, `SetBlobs`,
`Salter`, scalar reduction and curve routines in an isolated process. Go matches
the initial public point, password derivation, reduced scalars, both proofs and
session key byte-for-byte. Reciprocal synthetic-server tests verify all wire
rounds and old/new AES key boundaries. On 2026-10-22 an isolated instance of the
actual Linux recorder 26.1.7.3 changed its advertisement from mask 1 to mask 3
after the supported SDK password migration. The unmodified pure Go client then
completed mechanism-1 authentication and configuration retrieval. This adds
real-recorder negotiation evidence to the SDK differential fixtures; it does
not qualify every appliance model or recorder version.

## Real-recorder qualification and migration

The disposable recorder used fresh package files, private mount/PID/network
namespaces and loopback networking. It had no cameras or copied licence, user
database or configuration. Its one administrator account was provisioned with
the package's `useraccountsAdminBlank.xml` and `edvrpasswd`, using the same stdin
password flow as the installer. No password or verifier was fabricated for the
wire exchange. The original recorder's authentication configuration was untouched.

Before migration, fresh SDK sessions reported zero devices/cameras, one user,
full administrator access and `EVAPI_SecurePasswordsEnabled == 0`; the pure Go
client authenticated against the recorder's mask 1. The pinned SDK's exported
`EVAPI_MigrateSystemToSecurePasswords(handle)` returned zero. A fresh SDK session
then authenticated with the same credential and reported secure passwords
enabled. The pure Go client independently received mask 3, selected mechanism 1,
verified the server proof and retrieved authenticated configuration. Final
`TestLabSpakePlusRecorder` qualification passed four correct logins, including
configuration/status/licence reads on the first three, rejection of an incorrect
password, and a successful correct login afterward. Login plus reads took
85/29/24 ms in those three sequential observations; these are bounded local
samples, not WAN latency or capacity measurements.

The fresh unlicensed server exposed a licence/status-shape variant, now handled
without relaxing authentication or licence enforcement. The rebuilt private API
returned HTTP 200 for inventory and three health requests on both the isolated
unlicensed server and the original trial server. Isolated health calls took
22/23/24 ms; original-server calls took 21/20/20 ms. Affected Go transport, timing
and API race suites passed. Sanitized evidence and scope are recorded in
`spakeplus-validation.json` and `validation.md`.

This is a server-wide, one-way migration, not an account-level or TLS toggle.
The vendor documents it under Configure System > Security > Password
Strengthening and Augmented Authentication, explicitly marking it irreversible.
Use a disposable server for qualification, not a temporary account on a shared
recorder. [Vendor security-tab documentation](https://docs.johnsoncontrols.com/exacq/r/Exacq/en-US/exacqVision-Start-User-Manual/24.12/System-configuration/Configure-system-window/Security-tab)

Static corroboration in server `streampi.so` 26.1.7.3 (SHA-256
`ba826b563770bf067be8285cd6a6d14a2645b06de96f9ea0ce409c33364a09ab`):
`0xe6ea4..0xe6ec4` constructs `NegotiateMechanisms` as 1 or 3 from the
server's verifier setting. Its configuration update at `0x14bfad..0x14bfc2`
ignores writes of `UseVerifiers=0`. In the pinned SDK,
`CConnectionImpl::migrate_to_verifiers` at `0x27b1f0` generates verifiers for
cached users and writes `Users@UseVerifiers=1`; exported
`EVAPI_MigrateSystemToSecurePasswords` at `0x36f2c0` invokes that supported path.

## Exact exchange

All negotiation messages use packet type 2, subtype 5 and the existing
16-byte SPAKE blob wrapper: mechanism byte 1, little-endian blob lengths at
offsets 4 and 8, reserved bytes zero, followed by the two blobs.

| Sender | First blob | Second blob | Encryption key |
|---|---|---|---|
| Client | Compressed Edwards point X | UTF-8 username | Existing transport key |
| Server | Compressed Edwards point Y | Password salt | Existing transport key |
| Client | Client proof, 32 bytes | Exact echoed salt | Existing transport key |
| Server | Server proof, 32 bytes | Ignored by SDK | Existing transport key |
| Server, packet 2/2 | Final successful login response | Not a SPAKE wrapper | New session key |

After verifying the server proof, the client changes its transmit key without
sending another negotiation packet. Its receive key changes immediately before
decrypting the successful 2/2 acknowledgement. A premature 2/2 response fails.
This differs from mechanism 0, which receives the server proof with its first
challenge and sends the client proof plus echoed server proof before rekeying.

## Group operations and password derivation

Points are the canonical 32-byte compressed Edwards25519 encoding, including
the x-sign bit. They are not X25519 Montgomery u-coordinates. The client's
32 random bytes are clamped with `x[0] &= 248`, `x[31] &= 63`, and
`x[31] |= 64`. Its initial message is unmasked: `X = xG`.

The fixed masking point N has encoding:

```text
10e3df0ae37d8e7a99b5fe74b44672103dbddcbd06af680d71329a11693bc778
```

Run Argon2i version 1.3 with the password bytes and server salt: time cost 2,
memory 16,384 KiB, four lanes, output 64 bytes. Interpret each 32-byte half as a
little-endian integer and independently reduce it modulo the Edwards prime
subgroup order, yielding w0 and w1. Do not clamp these two password scalars.

The server point is `Y = yG + w0N`. The client computes:

```text
Q = Y - w0N
Z = xQ
V = w1Q
```

Define H as SHA-256 of each field's ASCII decimal byte length immediately
followed by that field's bytes, concatenated without delimiters. Then:

```text
clientProof = H(username, X, Y, Z, V)
serverProof = H(serverSerial, X, Y, Z, V)
sessionHash = H(username, serverSerial, X, Y, Z, V)
AES128Key   = sessionHash[0:16]
```

An empty server serial is a zero-length first field in `serverProof`; unlike
mechanism 0, this path does not substitute a two-identity proof. Raw UTF-8 and
embedded NUL password bytes were included in the SDK fixtures; no Unicode
normalization is introduced.

## Bounds and checks

The implementation accepts a 32-byte canonical peer point and salts from 8 to
1024 bytes. Argon2 parameters are fixed locally, never supplied by the peer.
At most one derivation occurs per authentication attempt. The unmasked point Q
must be nonidentity and in the prime-order subgroup; identity, pure torsion and
mixed-order peers never release a session key. Validation is on Q, since N has
an order-eight torsion component. Invalid Q is deliberately rejected only when
the server proof arrives: the preceding client message contains a random
32-byte dummy proof and the exact salt echo. Rejecting earlier would reveal
whether the server-selected torsion component equals `w0 mod 8`, creating a
password-partition oracle. Every challenge performs the same projection,
nonidentity selection, shared-point calculations and random-proof generation;
constant-time selection chooses the real proof only for a valid Q. A real proof
computed from a substituted generator must never be emitted, because its shared
points `Z=X` and `V=w1G` would provide an offline password verifier. Malformed
wire encodings still fail immediately because their validity is independent of
the password. The second server-proof blob is ignored as in the SDK but limited
to 1024 bytes.

Proof comparison is constant time. Failed or repeated messages consume the
exchange. Ephemeral scalars, derived password bytes, shared-point byte strings,
proofs and retained session material are cleared when they are no longer needed.
Context cancellation closes the transport; the fixed Argon2 invocation itself
is not interruptible, so cancellation can wait for that bounded computation.

Curve operations use the pinned pure Go
[`filippo.io/edwards25519` v1.2.0](https://pkg.go.dev/filippo.io/edwards25519@v1.2.0),
which exposes scalar multiplication, point subtraction and canonical encodings.
Argon2i uses the repository's existing `golang.org/x/crypto/argon2` dependency.
Neither requires CGO or a vendor library at runtime.

## SDK oracle and reproducibility

The binary identity is the SHA-256 recorded in `auth-research.md`. The oracle
script refuses a different binary. ELF virtual addresses before ASLR:

| Routine or data | Address | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| `Spake2PlusClient<Point25519>::Process` | `0x25fda0` | State machine, both shared points, proof/key hashes |
| Initial point generation within Process | `0x260260` | Random scalar clamping, unmasked X |
| `Spake2PlusClient::SetBlobs` | `0x25e1d0` | Challenge Y/salt, then server proof |
| `verifier_utils::Salter` | `0x1f3500` | Exact Argon2i parameters |
| `x25519_sc_reduce` | `0x234340` | Little-endian reduction of each password half |
| N precomputation data | `0x6d33d0` | Encoded point recovered using scalar one |
| `PakePeer::CalculateHash` | `0x25f2a0` | Decimal-length transcript hashing |
| `production_connection::Read` | `0x25b180`–`0x25b22c` | SetBlobs/Process and echoed second blob |
| Completion branch | `0x25b630`–`0x25b6ac` | Mode 1 rekeys without sending another proof |

Run `spakeplus-oracle.py` with `uv run` on Linux x64 with the pinned library and
its dependency directory in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. It uses synthetic values only,
opens no recorder connection and changes no configuration. It checks a randomly
generated SDK initial point, then replaces that ephemeral randomness with fixed
test scalars to produce reproducible fixtures. It checks the SDK's bad-proof
rejection and successful proof processing before printing fixture JSON.

The script intentionally runs in a disposable process: its recovered C++ object
layout is solely an oracle mechanism and never a wire-layout assumption or
production dependency. `pkg/exacq/testdata/spakeplus.json` is its immutable
output. The Go tests additionally reject malformed encodings and low-order
points and exercise cancellation, strongest-mechanism selection, premature
success, bad server proofs and receive-key transitions. An adversarial test
tries all eight torsion classes of a server-selected challenge: every class
receives the same-shaped client message, while the seven invalid classes reject
even the test's copy of the internal expected server proof. This regression
reproduced the earlier immediate rejection in exactly seven of eight classes.
